```{r cars}

data <- read_xls("ps2_data.xls")

colnames(data)[4:5] <- c("ret_inc_div", "ret_exc_div")

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(div_yield = ((1 + ret_inc_div) / (1 + ret_exc_div)) - 1,
         log_div_yield = log(div_yield),
         div_growth = div_yield/lag(div_yield, 1) * (1 + ret_exc_div),
         lead_logret = log(1 + lead(ret_inc_div, 1)),
         lead_logdy = lead(log_div_yield, 1),
         lead_logdg = log(lead(div_growth, 1))) %>% 
  as.data.table()

data1 <- na.omit(data)

dg_dy <- lm(lead_logdg ~ log_div_yield, data = data1)
ldy_dy <- lm(lead_logdy ~ log_div_yield, data = data1)
r_dy <- lm(lead_logret ~ log_div_yield, data = data1)
p <- mean(1/data1$div_yield) / (mean(1/data1$div_yield) + 1) # p = 0.9666094

results <- matrix(NA, 2, 3, dimnames = list(c("lm", "implied"), c("Beta_d", "Beta_y", "Beta_r")))
results[1,1] <- coef(dg_dy)[2]
results[1,2] <- coef(ldy_dy)[2]
results[1,3] <- coef(r_dy)[2]
results[2,1] <- coef(r_dy)[2] - 1 + (p * coef(ldy_dy)[2])
results[2,2] <- (1 - coef(r_dy)[2] + coef(dg_dy)[2]) / p
results[2,3] <- 1 + coef(dg_dy)[2] - (p * coef(ldy_dy)[2])

print(summary(r_dy))

print(round(results, 5))

# The implied value of B_r is rather close to its regression estimate. This suggest that the value of B_d and B_y could closely predict what we observe from running the regression of dividend yields on future returns. 

# Dividend growth is not predictable as value of B_d is close to zero i.e. cashflow channel does not explain the time-variation of dividend yield. We could conclude that most predictability is coming from expected return predictability / time-variation discount rate. 

```
